results.summary: Test suite passes in existing reports and JaCoCo is configured, but the tests fail the specialized test-quality standard because every test method violates the required `should_ExpectedResult_when_Condition` naming pattern, AAA structure is not explicit, and one public exception-handler method is untested.

findings.title: Service test methods do not follow `should_ExpectedResult_when_Condition`
findings.description: All three service test methods use behavior-style names without the required `should_ExpectedResult_when_Condition` camelCase pattern, so the method names do not comply with the review agent's specification-as-test-name rule.
findings.evidence: `greetNormalizesRepeatedWhitespace`, `greetRejectsBlankName`, and `greetRejectsNullName` are annotated with `@Test` but do not start with `should_..._when_...`.
findings.suggestedFix: Rename to names such as `should_returnGreeting_when_nameContainsRepeatedWhitespace`, `should_throwIllegalArgumentException_when_nameIsBlank`, and `should_throwIllegalArgumentException_when_nameIsNull`.

findings.title: Controller test methods do not follow `should_ExpectedResult_when_Condition`
findings.description: All five controller test methods violate the required test naming convention. This weakens the tests as executable specifications and is classified High by the agent definition.
findings.evidence: Methods include `healthReturnsUp`, `greetByQueryReturnsGreeting`, `greetByBodyReturnsGreeting`, `greetByQueryRejectsBlankName`, and `greetByBodyRejectsBlankName`.
findings.suggestedFix: Rename to names such as `should_returnUp_when_healthEndpointRequested`, `should_returnGreeting_when_validQueryNameProvided`, and `should_returnBadRequest_when_bodyNameIsBlank`.

findings.title: Service tests do not clearly separate Arrange, Act, and Assert
findings.description: The service tests combine Act and Assert in a single AssertJ expression and have no clear Arrange / Act / Assert separation by comments or blank lines. The error-path tests pass the method invocation directly into `assertThatThrownBy`, which obscures the single Act step under the agent's strict AAA standard.
findings.evidence: Example: line 14 calls `greetingService.greet(...)` inside `assertThat(...)`; lines 20 and 27 call `greetingService.greet(...)` inside `assertThatThrownBy(...)`.
findings.suggestedFix: Use explicit blocks, e.g. arrange input, act with `var result = greetingService.greet(name)` or `var thrown = catchThrowable(() -> greetingService.greet(name))`, then assert the result or throwable separately.

findings.title: Controller tests combine request execution and assertions in one chain
findings.description: The MockMvc tests execute the HTTP request and assert the response in one fluent chain without explicit Arrange / Act / Assert separation. Under the review standard, the Act block should be a single visible method call and assertions should be clearly separated.
findings.evidence: Each test uses `mockMvc.perform(...).andExpect(...)` directly, for example lines 26-28 and 40-46.
findings.suggestedFix: Assign `ResultActions result = mockMvc.perform(...)` in the Act block, then run `result.andExpect(...)` in the Assert block. Add concise `// Arrange`, `// Act`, `// Assert` comments or clear blank-line separation.

findings.title: Public exception-handler method is not covered
findings.description: JaCoCo shows `GlobalExceptionHandler.handleInvalidParameter(HandlerMethodValidationException)` at 0% coverage. The controller tests cover body validation and another query validation path, but not this public handler method, violating the agent rule that all public methods should be tested.
findings.evidence: `target/site/jacoco/com.codexskishop.sample.api/GlobalExceptionHandler.html` reports `handleInvalidParameter(HandlerMethodValidationException)` as 0% and line 37 as not covered.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a focused unit test for `GlobalExceptionHandler.handleInvalidParameter(...)` or an MVC scenario that actually raises `HandlerMethodValidationException`, then verify status 400 and the sanitized error response.

findings.title: Tests do not use `@DisplayName` descriptions
findings.description: None of the test methods include `@DisplayName`. The agent standard treats `@DisplayName` as the human-readable description layer for test specifications.
findings.evidence: `rg` found `@Test` methods in both test classes but no `@DisplayName` annotations.
findings.suggestedFix: Add `@DisplayName` to each test with concise human-readable behavior descriptions, in addition to renaming methods to the required pattern.

findings.title: Validation boundary cases for maximum name length are missing
findings.description: The API and request DTO enforce `@Size(max = 40)`, but tests only cover blank names. Boundary cases at 40 and 41 characters are not covered, and these are important for validation behavior.
findings.evidence: `greetByQuery` validates `@Size(max = 40)` and `GreetingRequest.name` has the same constraint, but `GreetingControllerTest` only tests blank query/body values.
findings.suggestedFix: Add parameterized controller tests using `@ParameterizedTest` and `@CsvSource` or `@ValueSource` for valid 40-character names and invalid 41-character names for both query and body paths.

results.summary: Resilience review of sample-java-code found no external HTTP clients, so retry/circuit-breaker/timeout/fallback checks for outbound calls are not applicable. The target fails the resilience baseline because Spring Boot Actuator liveness/readiness endpoints are not implemented, and graceful shutdown is not configured.

findings.title: Actuator liveness/readiness health endpoints are not implemented
findings.description: The application only defines a bespoke `/api/health` smoke endpoint and does not include Spring Boot Actuator or management health probe configuration. This means `/actuator/health` and `/actuator/health/readiness` are unavailable, so orchestration platforms cannot reliably distinguish liveness from readiness.
findings.evidence: Dependencies include validation, web, and test only; `spring-boot-starter-actuator` is absent. `sample-java-code/src/main/resources/application.yml:1` only configures server port and application name. `sample-java-code/src/main/java/com/codexskishop/sample/api/GreetingController.java:34` defines `/api/health`, not Actuator health groups.
findings.suggestedFix: Add `spring-boot-starter-actuator`, then configure health probes: `management.endpoints.web.exposure.include: health,info,metrics`, `management.endpoint.health.probes.enabled: true`, `management.health.livenessstate.enabled: true`, and `management.health.readinessstate.enabled: true`. Keep `/api/health` only as an optional smoke endpoint if needed.

findings.title: Graceful shutdown and shutdown phase timeout are not configured
findings.description: The application does not configure graceful shutdown, so termination can interrupt in-flight HTTP requests during deploys, restarts, or platform-driven rescheduling.
findings.evidence: `application.yml` only contains `server.port` and `spring.application.name`; it does not set `server.shutdown=graceful` or `spring.lifecycle.timeout-per-shutdown-phase`.
findings.suggestedFix: Configure `server.shutdown: graceful` and set an explicit `spring.lifecycle.timeout-per-shutdown-phase`, for example `20s`, then verify platform termination grace period is longer than the application shutdown timeout.

findings.title: Field injection with @Autowired is used in a test class
findings.description: The tech-lead checklist defines @Autowired field injection as a zero-tolerance prohibited pattern anywhere in the project. This test injects MockMvc through a mutable field instead of constructor injection.
findings.evidence:
@Autowired
private MockMvc mockMvc;
findings.suggestedFix: Use constructor injection in the JUnit test, for example: private final MockMvc mockMvc; GreetingControllerTest(@Autowired MockMvc mockMvc) { this.mockMvc = mockMvc; }

findings.title: Spring-managed service is directly instantiated
findings.description: GreetingService is annotated with @Service in production code, but the unit test creates it with new. The tech-lead checklist explicitly prohibits direct new instantiation of Service/Repository DI-target classes.
findings.evidence: private final GreetingService greetingService = new GreetingService();
findings.suggestedFix: Inject GreetingService from a Spring test context, or if this class is intended to be a pure non-DI unit, remove the Spring stereotype and wire it through an explicit bean/configuration boundary.

findings.title: Service layer returns an API DTO
findings.description: GreetingService imports and returns GreetingResponse from the api package. This couples the service layer to HTTP/API DTOs, while the Java AGENTS guidance assigns DTO conversion to controllers and orchestration/business behavior to services. The next service consumer would inherit API-layer types unnecessarily.
findings.suggestedFix: Have GreetingService return a service/domain value such as String, then create GreetingResponse in GreetingController: return new GreetingResponse(greetingService.greet(name));

findings.title: Service validation exception is not handled by the global API error policy
findings.description: GreetingService can throw IllegalArgumentException for invalid names, but GlobalExceptionHandler only handles Spring validation exceptions. If this service exception reaches the controller layer, the API will not use the same sanitized ErrorResponse contract.
findings.evidence: Handlers are registered for MethodArgumentNotValidException, HandlerMethodValidationException, and ConstraintViolationException only; GreetingService throws IllegalArgumentException at sample-java-code/src/main/java/com/codexskishop/sample/service/GreetingService.java:22.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a focused @ExceptionHandler(IllegalArgumentException.class) that returns the same sanitized 400 ErrorResponse, or replace the service exception with a domain-specific exception handled by the global advice.

findings.title: Service layer depends on API response DTO
findings.description: `GreetingService` imports and returns `GreetingResponse` from the web/API package. This creates an upward dependency from the service layer to the presentation/API layer, violating the intended dependency direction where controllers depend on services, and DTO conversion stays at the controller/API boundary.
findings.evidence: Line 3 imports `com.codexskishop.sample.api.GreetingResponse`; line 19 exposes it as the service return type; line 24 constructs the API response DTO inside the service.
findings.suggestedFix: Have `GreetingService` return an application/domain value such as `String` or a service-level result type, then construct `GreetingResponse` in `GreetingController`. Alternatively, move API contract records into `dto/response` only if the architecture explicitly allows services to return DTOs.

findings.title: Web, DTO, and exception responsibilities are collapsed into one `api` package
findings.description: The review standard expects distinct packages such as `controller/`, `dto/request/`, `dto/response/`, `config/`, and `exception/` under the application base package. The target instead places controller, request DTO, response DTOs, error DTO, and `@RestControllerAdvice` together under `com.codexskishop.sample.api`, weakening package boundaries and making dependency rules harder to enforce.
findings.evidence: `GreetingController`, `GreetingRequest`, `GreetingResponse`, `HealthResponse`, `ErrorResponse`, and `GlobalExceptionHandler` all declare `package com.codexskishop.sample.api;`. The directory listing contains only `api/` and `service/` under `com/codexskishop/sample`.
findings.suggestedFix: Split files into conventional packages: controller classes under `controller`, request records under `dto/request`, response records under `dto/response`, and advice/error exception types under `exception`. If this sample intentionally uses `com.codexskishop.sample` instead of `com.skishop`, document that exception in the sample AGENTS or README.

findings.title: Security configuration is absent
findings.description: The architecture review criteria require a `SecurityConfig` with `@Configuration`, `@EnableWebSecurity`, and a `SecurityFilterChain` bean. The target has no `config` package or security configuration, and the Maven dependencies do not include Spring Security. Even for public sample endpoints, an explicit permit-list security configuration protects future endpoint additions from becoming unintentionally public.
findings.evidence: Dependencies include validation, web, and test only. No `spring-boot-starter-security` is declared, and no `sample-java-code/src/main/java/com/codexskishop/sample/config/SecurityConfig.java` exists.
findings.suggestedFix: Add `spring-boot-starter-security` and create `config/SecurityConfig.java` with an explicit `SecurityFilterChain`, permitting only intended public endpoints such as `/api/health` and sample greeting routes, then update MVC tests for the security behavior.

findings.title: Profile-specific configuration separation is missing
findings.description: Only a single `application.yml` exists, containing server port and application name. The review criteria call for common, development, and production profile separation, and future database/JPA/security settings should not be mixed into one file.
findings.evidence: The resources directory contains `application.yml` only; no `application-dev.yml` or `application-prod.yml` was present in the reviewed target files.
findings.suggestedFix: Keep common settings in `application.yml` and add profile-specific files such as `application-dev.yml` and `application-prod.yml` when environment-sensitive settings are introduced. For this sample, document if profile separation is intentionally out of scope.

findings.title: Greeting normalization and validation are implemented in the service layer instead of a domain object or value object
findings.description: GreetingService contains the rule for normalizing repeated whitespace and rejecting a blank normalized name. If this sample is intended to model domain behavior, the invariant should be encapsulated in a domain value object such as GreetingName, with the service only coordinating the use case. Confidence is medium because the target appears to be a deliberately small sample API rather than a SkiShop business domain.
findings.evidence: public GreetingResponse greet(String name) { String normalizedName = normalizeName(name); if (normalizedName.isBlank()) { throw new IllegalArgumentException("name must not be blank"); } return new GreetingResponse("Hello, %s!".formatted(normalizedName)); }
findings.suggestedFix: Introduce an immutable domain value object, for example `record GreetingName(String value)`, that performs normalization and blank validation in its compact constructor. Then let `GreetingService` delegate to that value object and map the result to the API response.

findings.title: REST error responses do not use Spring ProblemDetail / ResponseEntityExceptionHandler
findings.description: The REST exception handler returns a custom ErrorResponse record instead of Spring Boot ProblemDetail and does not extend ResponseEntityExceptionHandler. This violates the API endpoint review standard for RFC 9457-style error responses and makes error contracts harder to standardize across future endpoints.
findings.evidence: @RestControllerAdvice public class GlobalExceptionHandler { ... public ResponseEntity<ErrorResponse> handleInvalidBody(...)
findings.suggestedFix: Change the handler to extend ResponseEntityExceptionHandler and return ProblemDetail or ResponseEntity<ProblemDetail>; include status, title, and sanitized detail fields consistently.

findings.title: Invalid binding cases are not fully handled by the centralized error handler
findings.description: The handler covers body validation, method validation, and constraint violations, but it does not handle common request binding failures such as missing required query parameters or malformed JSON. Those cases will fall through to Spring Boot's default error handling instead of the sample API's consistent sanitized response shape.
findings.evidence: Only MethodArgumentNotValidException, HandlerMethodValidationException, and ConstraintViolationException are registered with @ExceptionHandler.
findings.suggestedFix: Add centralized handling through ResponseEntityExceptionHandler overrides such as handleMissingServletRequestParameter and handleHttpMessageNotReadable, returning the same ProblemDetail contract.

findings.title: Stack trace suppression is not explicitly configured
findings.description: application.yml does not explicitly set server.error.include-stacktrace=never. Spring Boot defaults usually avoid exposing stack traces, so this is not evidence of an active leak, but the review standard asks for this to be verifiable in configuration.
findings.evidence: server: port: 8081; no server.error.include-stacktrace setting is present.
findings.suggestedFix: Add server.error.include-stacktrace: never, and consider server.error.include-message: never or an equivalent sanitized setting for default error paths.

findings.title: Field injection with @Autowired is used in a Java test class
findings.description: The standards prohibit @Autowired field injection in all .java files. GreetingControllerTest injects MockMvc through a mutable field instead of constructor injection.
findings.evidence:
@Autowired
private MockMvc mockMvc;
findings.suggestedFix: Use constructor injection in the test class, for example a final MockMvc field initialized by an @Autowired constructor.

findings.title: DI-managed service is directly instantiated
findings.description: GreetingService is annotated with @Service, but the test creates it with new GreetingService(). The standards prohibit direct instantiation of DI-managed Service classes in .java files.
findings.evidence: private final GreetingService greetingService = new GreetingService();
findings.suggestedFix: Inject GreetingService from a Spring test context, or separate pure domain logic from the Spring-managed service and instantiate only the non-DI component directly.

findings.title: Service has no corresponding interface
findings.description: The DI standards require all Service/Repository classes to have corresponding interfaces. GreetingService is a concrete @Service and GreetingController depends on the concrete class.
findings.evidence:
@Service
public class GreetingService {
findings.suggestedFix: Introduce an interface such as GreetingUseCase or GreetingServicePort with greet(String name), implement it in GreetingService, and inject the interface into GreetingController.

findings.title: Public service parameter has ambiguous nullability contract
findings.description: GreetingService.greet(String name) accepts an unannotated String, while normalizeName explicitly handles null. The standards require @Nullable/@NonNull annotations where nullability is ambiguous.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare the contract explicitly, for example annotate name as @NonNull and reject null immediately, or annotate it as @Nullable and document that null is treated as invalid input.

findings.title: Java 21 virtual threads are not enabled
findings.description: The project targets Java 21, but the Spring Boot configuration does not enable virtual threads. Under this review profile, `spring.threads.virtual.enabled=true` is expected so synchronous request handling can use lightweight request threads and avoid platform-thread scaling limits.
findings.evidence: `spring.application.name` is configured, but there is no `spring.threads.virtual.enabled: true` entry in `application.yml`.
findings.suggestedFix:
Add `spring.threads.virtual.enabled: true` under the `spring` section, for example:

spring:
  threads:
    virtual:
      enabled: true
  application:
    name: sample-java-code

findings.title: Global exception handler does not return RFC 7807 ProblemDetail
findings.description: The global handler returns a custom ErrorResponse body instead of Spring Boot ProblemDetail. This breaks the review requirement for consistent RFC 7807/RFC 9457 error responses and makes error contracts diverge from standard Spring Boot 3.x behavior.
findings.evidence: Handler methods return ResponseEntity<ErrorResponse>, and badRequest() creates new ErrorResponse("Request validation failed.", Instant.now()).
findings.suggestedFix: Change handlers to return ProblemDetail, for example ProblemDetail.forStatusAndDetail(HttpStatus.BAD_REQUEST, "Request validation failed."); set a stable title and avoid exposing internal exception details.

findings.title: No catch-all sanitized exception handler
findings.description: GlobalExceptionHandler only maps validation exceptions. Unexpected runtime exceptions will fall through to Spring Boot default handling instead of a controlled sanitized ProblemDetail response, which weakens MTTR and consistency for 500 responses.
findings.evidence: Only MethodArgumentNotValidException, HandlerMethodValidationException, and ConstraintViolationException are handled.
findings.suggestedFix: Add @ExceptionHandler(Exception.class) that logs the exception with stack trace server-side and returns a sanitized ProblemDetail with HttpStatus.INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR. Also explicitly set server.error.include-stacktrace=never in application.yml.

findings.title: Service throws generic IllegalArgumentException without API mapping
findings.description: GreetingService throws IllegalArgumentException for a domain/input failure, but there is no exception hierarchy or @ExceptionHandler mapping for it. If this exception reaches the API boundary, clients receive inconsistent default error handling rather than a deliberate 400/422 response.
findings.evidence: throw new IllegalArgumentException("name must not be blank"); no matching IllegalArgumentException handler exists in GlobalExceptionHandler.
findings.suggestedFix: Introduce a small application exception hierarchy such as ValidationException or BusinessException and map it in @RestControllerAdvice, or explicitly handle IllegalArgumentException as BAD_REQUEST with ProblemDetail.

findings.title: Missing correlation ID filter and MDC propagation
findings.description: No request filter/interceptor assigns X-Correlation-Id, stores it in MDC, returns it in the response header, or clears MDC after the request. Production incidents become harder to trace across request logs.
findings.evidence: Search of sample-java-code found no MDC, CorrelationId, or X-Correlation-Id implementation; the application has only the SpringBootApplication entry point and API/service classes.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a OncePerRequestFilter that reads or generates X-Correlation-Id, calls MDC.put("correlationId", value), sets the response header, delegates the chain, and clears MDC in finally.

findings.title: No production JSON Logback configuration
findings.description: The module has no logback-spring.xml and no logstash-logback-encoder dependency, so logs are not configured for structured JSON output or MDC correlation ID emission.
findings.evidence: Dependencies include validation, web, and test only; no logstash-logback-encoder. application.yml also contains no logging pattern including correlationId.
findings.suggestedFix: Add logstash-logback-encoder where justified for production logging, create logback-spring.xml JSON appenders, and include correlationId from MDC in the log fields.

findings.title: Spring Boot Actuator/Micrometer endpoints are not enabled
findings.description: The sample application does not include spring-boot-starter-actuator or management endpoint configuration. Health and metrics visibility relies on a custom /api/health endpoint only, leaving standard operational telemetry unavailable.
findings.evidence: Dependencies list spring-boot-starter-validation, spring-boot-starter-web, and spring-boot-starter-test; no spring-boot-starter-actuator is present.
findings.suggestedFix: Add spring-boot-starter-actuator and configure management.endpoints.web.exposure.include for required endpoints such as health, info, metrics, and prometheus if needed.

findings.title: No Spring Security dependency or SecurityFilterChain is present
findings.description: The application depends on Spring Web and Validation only, and no SecurityFilterChain configuration was found. As a result, authorization rules, CSRF/session policy, authentication configuration, and security headers are absent rather than explicitly controlled by the application standard.
findings.evidence: The dependency block contains spring-boot-starter-validation, spring-boot-starter-web, and spring-boot-starter-test only. Repository search found no SecurityFilterChain, authorizeHttpRequests, csrf, sessionManagement, headers, or spring-boot-starter-security entries under sample-java-code.
findings.suggestedFix: Add spring-boot-starter-security and a dedicated @Configuration class defining SecurityFilterChain. At minimum explicitly permit only health/public endpoints, protect non-public API routes, configure CSRF/session policy appropriate for REST or MVC, and set security headers via headers(...).

findings.title: Stack trace exposure is not explicitly disabled
findings.description: The application configuration does not set server.error.include-stacktrace=never. Spring Boot defaults are generally safe, but the review standard requires this to be explicit in application configuration and production profile configuration to prevent accidental stack trace exposure through profile drift or future overrides.
findings.evidence: application.yml only sets server.port and spring.application.name; there is no server.error.include-stacktrace entry.
findings.suggestedFix: Add server.error.include-stacktrace: never to common configuration and repeat or enforce it in production profile configuration.

findings.title: Production profile configuration is missing
findings.description: Only application.yml exists under src/main/resources. The review standard expects common, development, and production configuration separation, including production-safe logging and security settings.
findings.evidence: src/main/resources contains application.yml only; no application-prod.yml or application-dev.yml was found. The existing file contains only server.port and spring.application.name.
findings.suggestedFix: Add application-prod.yml with production-safe settings such as logging.level.root: WARN, server.error.include-stacktrace: never, explicit server.server-header handling if desired, and documented HTTPS termination or server.ssl settings. Add application-dev.yml only for development-specific overrides.

findings.category: A01 Broken Access Control / E Elevation of Privilege
findings.title: No Spring Security baseline or default-deny authorization fallback
findings.description: The application includes Spring Web and Validation but no Spring Security dependency or SecurityFilterChain. All current /api endpoints are public by framework default, and there is no explicit permitlist plus anyRequest().authenticated() fallback. Current endpoints are low-sensitivity, but this does not meet the repository security standard and creates a high-risk baseline for future API expansion.
findings.evidence: Dependencies include spring-boot-starter-validation, spring-boot-starter-web, and spring-boot-starter-test only; no spring-boot-starter-security or SecurityFilterChain exists in the reviewed target files.
findings.suggestedFix: Add spring-boot-starter-security and a SecurityFilterChain that explicitly permitlists public endpoints such as /api/health, then applies .anyRequest().authenticated(). Add role checks for any admin or user-specific endpoints when introduced.

findings.category: Security Headers / A07 XSS Defense in Depth
findings.title: Security headers are not configured
findings.description: Because no Spring Security header configuration or equivalent filter exists, the app does not explicitly set CSP, X-Frame-Options, HSTS, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, or X-Content-Type-Options. This weakens defense in depth against XSS impact, clickjacking, content sniffing, and transport downgrade risks.
findings.evidence: application.yml only sets server.port and spring.application.name. No header policy is configured elsewhere in the reviewed source.
findings.suggestedFix: Configure headers via Spring Security, for example contentTypeOptions, frameOptions().deny(), contentSecurityPolicy("default-src 'self'"), referrerPolicy(STRICT_ORIGIN_WHEN_CROSS_ORIGIN), permissionsPolicy, and HSTS when TLS is used. Also define the deployment TLS termination model.

findings.category: A05 Security Misconfiguration / A09 Error Handling
findings.title: Production error disclosure hardening is not explicit
findings.description: The global exception handler sanitizes validation errors, but application.yml does not explicitly pin Spring Boot error disclosure settings. Spring Boot defaults are usually safe for stack traces, so this is not confirmed leakage, but relying on defaults leaves room for profile or parameter drift exposing exception details.
findings.evidence: No server.error.include-stacktrace, server.error.include-message, server.error.include-binding-errors, or server.server-header settings are present. GlobalExceptionHandler handles validation-related exceptions only.
findings.suggestedFix: Add production-safe settings such as server.error.include-stacktrace=never, server.error.include-message=never, server.error.include-binding-errors=never, and server.server-header=blank. Consider a generic @ExceptionHandler that returns a sanitized error body for unexpected exceptions without exposing exception messages.

findings.category: D Denial of Service / Rate Limiting
findings.title: Public endpoints have no rate limiting or explicit request-size hardening
findings.description: The API accepts unauthenticated GET and POST requests and has no rate limiting, connection timeout, or explicit request-size limits in the reviewed configuration. Bean Validation caps the logical name field at 40 characters, but it does not stop request flooding or oversized HTTP bodies before request parsing.
findings.evidence: GET /api/health, GET /api/greetings, and POST /api/greetings are public controller methods. No rate limiting filter or server size/timeout settings were found in the target files.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a small rate-limiting filter or gateway policy for public endpoints, and set appropriate server limits such as max request size, connection timeout, and keep-alive timeout. Keep endpoint-specific validation as a second layer.

findings.title: Spring Boot parent version does not match required 3.2.x line
findings.description: The review standard requires spring-boot-starter-parent version 3.2.x, but the module inherits Spring Boot 3.5.8. This is a policy mismatch for BOM-managed dependency alignment in this review scope.
findings.evidence: <version>3.5.8</version> under org.springframework.boot:spring-boot-starter-parent
findings.suggestedFix: Change the parent version to an approved Spring Boot 3.2.x release, then run the full Maven test/verification suite to catch API or managed-version differences.

findings.title: Project artifact uses a SNAPSHOT version
findings.description: The module declares version 0.0.1-SNAPSHOT. The agent policy has zero tolerance for SNAPSHOT versions in production/public-release dependency management because they undermine reproducible artifact resolution and release stability.
findings.evidence: <version>0.0.1-SNAPSHOT</version>
findings.suggestedFix: Use a stable release version such as 0.0.1 for publishable/reviewed artifacts, or isolate SNAPSHOT usage to non-production development profiles with an explicit release process.

findings.title: Required Maven encoding properties are missing
findings.description: The POM declares XML encoding but does not define project.build.sourceEncoding or project.reporting.outputEncoding. The dependency-management build checklist expects both to be UTF-8 for consistent source and report generation across environments.
findings.evidence: <properties> contains java.version and jacoco.version only; no project.build.sourceEncoding or project.reporting.outputEncoding.
findings.suggestedFix: Add <project.build.sourceEncoding>UTF-8</project.build.sourceEncoding> and <project.reporting.outputEncoding>UTF-8</project.reporting.outputEncoding> to the properties block.

findings.title: Service test methods do not follow `should_ExpectedResult_when_Condition`
findings.description: All three service test methods use behavior-style names without the required `should_ExpectedResult_when_Condition` camelCase pattern, so the method names do not comply with the review agent's specification-as-test-name rule.
findings.evidence: `greetNormalizesRepeatedWhitespace`, `greetRejectsBlankName`, and `greetRejectsNullName` are annotated with `@Test` but do not start with `should_..._when_...`.
findings.suggestedFix: Rename to names such as `should_returnGreeting_when_nameContainsRepeatedWhitespace`, `should_throwIllegalArgumentException_when_nameIsBlank`, and `should_throwIllegalArgumentException_when_nameIsNull`.

findings.title: Controller test methods do not follow `should_ExpectedResult_when_Condition`
findings.description: All five controller test methods violate the required test naming convention. This weakens the tests as executable specifications and is classified High by the agent definition.
findings.evidence: Methods include `healthReturnsUp`, `greetByQueryReturnsGreeting`, `greetByBodyReturnsGreeting`, `greetByQueryRejectsBlankName`, and `greetByBodyRejectsBlankName`.
findings.suggestedFix: Rename to names such as `should_returnUp_when_healthEndpointRequested`, `should_returnGreeting_when_validQueryNameProvided`, and `should_returnBadRequest_when_bodyNameIsBlank`.

findings.title: Service tests do not clearly separate Arrange, Act, and Assert
findings.description: The service tests combine Act and Assert in a single AssertJ expression and have no clear Arrange / Act / Assert separation by comments or blank lines. The error-path tests pass the method invocation directly into `assertThatThrownBy`, which obscures the single Act step under the agent's strict AAA standard.
findings.evidence: Example: line 14 calls `greetingService.greet(...)` inside `assertThat(...)`; lines 20 and 27 call `greetingService.greet(...)` inside `assertThatThrownBy(...)`.
findings.suggestedFix: Use explicit blocks, e.g. arrange input, act with `var result = greetingService.greet(name)` or `var thrown = catchThrowable(() -> greetingService.greet(name))`, then assert the result or throwable separately.

findings.title: Controller tests combine request execution and assertions in one chain
findings.description: The MockMvc tests execute the HTTP request and assert the response in one fluent chain without explicit Arrange / Act / Assert separation. Under the review standard, the Act block should be a single visible method call and assertions should be clearly separated.
findings.evidence: Each test uses `mockMvc.perform(...).andExpect(...)` directly, for example lines 26-28 and 40-46.
findings.suggestedFix: Assign `ResultActions result = mockMvc.perform(...)` in the Act block, then run `result.andExpect(...)` in the Assert block. Add concise `// Arrange`, `// Act`, `// Assert` comments or clear blank-line separation.

findings.title: Public exception-handler method is not covered
findings.description: JaCoCo shows `GlobalExceptionHandler.handleInvalidParameter(HandlerMethodValidationException)` at 0% coverage. The controller tests cover body validation and another query validation path, but not this public handler method, violating the agent rule that all public methods should be tested.
findings.evidence: `target/site/jacoco/com.codexskishop.sample.api/GlobalExceptionHandler.html` reports `handleInvalidParameter(HandlerMethodValidationException)` as 0% and line 37 as not covered.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a focused unit test for `GlobalExceptionHandler.handleInvalidParameter(...)` or an MVC scenario that actually raises `HandlerMethodValidationException`, then verify status 400 and the sanitized error response.

findings.title: Tests do not use `@DisplayName` descriptions
findings.description: None of the test methods include `@DisplayName`. The agent standard treats `@DisplayName` as the human-readable description layer for test specifications.
findings.evidence: `rg` found `@Test` methods in both test classes but no `@DisplayName` annotations.
findings.suggestedFix: Add `@DisplayName` to each test with concise human-readable behavior descriptions, in addition to renaming methods to the required pattern.

findings.title: Validation boundary cases for maximum name length are missing
findings.description: The API and request DTO enforce `@Size(max = 40)`, but tests only cover blank names. Boundary cases at 40 and 41 characters are not covered, and these are important for validation behavior.
findings.evidence: `greetByQuery` validates `@Size(max = 40)` and `GreetingRequest.name` has the same constraint, but `GreetingControllerTest` only tests blank query/body values.
findings.suggestedFix: Add parameterized controller tests using `@ParameterizedTest` and `@CsvSource` or `@ValueSource` for valid 40-character names and invalid 41-character names for both query and body paths.

findings.title: Actuator liveness/readiness health endpoints are not implemented
findings.description: The application only defines a bespoke `/api/health` smoke endpoint and does not include Spring Boot Actuator or management health probe configuration. This means `/actuator/health` and `/actuator/health/readiness` are unavailable, so orchestration platforms cannot reliably distinguish liveness from readiness.
findings.evidence: Dependencies include validation, web, and test only; `spring-boot-starter-actuator` is absent. `sample-java-code/src/main/resources/application.yml:1` only configures server port and application name. `sample-java-code/src/main/java/com/codexskishop/sample/api/GreetingController.java:34` defines `/api/health`, not Actuator health groups.
findings.suggestedFix: Add `spring-boot-starter-actuator`, then configure health probes: `management.endpoints.web.exposure.include: health,info,metrics`, `management.endpoint.health.probes.enabled: true`, `management.health.livenessstate.enabled: true`, and `management.health.readinessstate.enabled: true`. Keep `/api/health` only as an optional smoke endpoint if needed.

findings.title: Graceful shutdown and shutdown phase timeout are not configured
findings.description: The application does not configure graceful shutdown, so termination can interrupt in-flight HTTP requests during deploys, restarts, or platform-driven rescheduling.
findings.evidence: `application.yml` only contains `server.port` and `spring.application.name`; it does not set `server.shutdown=graceful` or `spring.lifecycle.timeout-per-shutdown-phase`.
findings.suggestedFix: Configure `server.shutdown: graceful` and set an explicit `spring.lifecycle.timeout-per-shutdown-phase`, for example `20s`, then verify platform termination grace period is longer than the application shutdown timeout.
